mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level consistently compresses equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The inverse relationship between FEDFUNDS and returns holds across multiple economic cycles without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no inverse correlation with 20-day returns: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window or t-test p-value > 0.05 for returns when FEDFUNDS is below median.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 8.5%, it signals an imminent economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened recession risk.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 8.5% occurs in 10 consecutive instances, yet 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deceleration in GDP growth (GDPC1) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a deepening recession, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (GDPC1 growth < 2% AND UNRATE > 8.0%) occurs in 15 instances, but returns are positive in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising 3-monthly), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns due to increased discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and 3-month rise > 0.5%) occur in 10 instances, yet 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) level signals strong economic activity, compressing risk premiums and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO level shows no positive correlation with 60-day returns: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window or t-test p-value > 0.05 for returns when INDPRO is above median.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 700.0 thousand units, it indicates a housing market collapse, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer confidence.
failure_condition: HOUST < 700.0 occurs in 10 consecutive instances, yet 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05 from t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Weak employment growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.5%) combined with high unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%) signals labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (PAYEMS growth < 0.5% AND UNRATE > 8.0%) occurs in 15 instances, but returns are positive in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95.0, it indicates a manufacturing slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings visibility.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 95.0 occurs in 10 consecutive instances, yet 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases (p-value > 0.05).
